text:
Travis Konecny's season has been more noise than hockey. Daily Faceoff reported in October that the Flyers would explore asking him to waive or loosen his no-movement clause, a later report described a rift between Philadelphia's veterans and its kids, and Charlie O'Connor, who covers the team, wrote that he'd be shocked if Konecny resented Porter Martone in particular. This week he spoke to the beat in Ottawa about all of it, and O'Connor said he spoke positively about the young players.

On the ice he has six points in 14 games, shooting 6.9% after years around his talent range of 13 to 14%. Some of that is luck we'd expect to turn: the Flyers have scored 7.9 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and he's pointless in four straight on 2.7 expected goals. Some of it isn't. His ice time is down almost two minutes over his last 10, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more with him on the ice last season than with almost any forward. He's 29, with 544 career points before this year, all of them in orange.
